title: Platelet aggregometry assay for evaluating the effects of platelet agonists and antiplatelet compounds on platelet function in vitro
author: Tsoupras, Zabetakis, et al.
materials: PAF is purchased as a crystalline substance (Sigma Aldrich, Wicklow, Ireland). Dilute the PAF in an appropriate amount of a chloroform/methanol (1:1 v/v) solution so that the stock concentration is 10−4 M, which should then be aliquoted for storage at −20 °C. When ready for use, the aliquoted stock solutions should be evaporated under a stream of nitrogen and re-dissolved in BSA-saline (2.5 mg BSA/mL 0.9% saline). This should then be serially diluted in BSA-saline to obtain solutions of PAF dissolved in BSA-saline with a final concentration in the cuvette ranging from 2.6 × 10−8 to 2.6 × 10−5 mol/L.

Crystalline standard active thrombin (Sigma Aldrich, Wicklow, Ireland) should be dissolved in saline, so that the stock concentration is 0.1 U/μL and this solution can be aliquoted for storage at −80 °C. When ready for use, the aliquoted stock solutions should be diluted in appropriate amounts of saline to obtain solutions of thrombin with a final concentration in the aggregometer cuvette ranging from 0.01mU/μL to 1mU/μL.

steps.title: Prepare PAF stock solution
steps.instruction: Dilute crystalline PAF in chloroform/methanol (1:1 v/v) to a 10⁻⁴ M stock, aliquot and store at –20 °C; when needed evaporate under nitrogen, re‑dissolve in BSA‑saline (2.5 mg BSA/mL 0.9 % saline) and serially dilute in the same buffer to obtain cuvette concentrations ranging from 2.6 × 10⁻⁸ to 2.6 × 10⁻⁵ M.

steps.title: Prepare thrombin stock solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve crystalline thrombin in saline to a stock concentration of 0.1 U/µL, aliquot and store at –80 °C; before use dilute the aliquot in saline to achieve cuvette concentrations of 0.01 mU/µL to 1 mU/µL.

steps.title: Collect blood and prepare PRP
steps.instruction: Have volunteers fast ≥8 h, draw blood from the median cubital or cephalic vein with a 20 G safety needle into 0.106 M sodium citrate monovettes (1:10 citrate:blood), invert three times, centrifuge at 194 × g for 18 min at 24 °C without brake, transfer the supernatant platelet‑rich plasma to polypropylene tubes and keep at 24 °C.

steps.title: Obtain platelet‑poor plasma
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the remaining material in the original monovette at 1465 × g for 20 min at 24 °C without brake to collect platelet‑poor plasma, and keep it at 24 °C.

steps.title: Adjust platelet count to 5×10⁵/µL
steps.instruction: Measure absorbance of 1 mL PRP and 1 mL PPP at 530 nm (PPP as blank); an absorbance of 0.8 corresponds to 500 000 platelets/µL. Add the calculated volume of PPP to PRP to reach this concentration.

steps.title: Set up aggregometer cuvettes
steps.instruction: Add 250 µL PPP to a glass aggregometer cuvette (spacer optional, no stirrer) and place it in the instrument well; add 250 µL PRP to a second glass cuvette, insert a disposable stirrer, set stirrer speed to 1200 rpm (1000 rpm acceptable), and pre‑warm the cuvette to 37 °C.

steps.title: Calibrate instrument and baseline
steps.instruction: Automatically zero PRP against PPP according to the manufacturer (set 100 % transmission then 0 %); after calibration wait 30 s to obtain a stable baseline.

steps.title: Add agonist and record aggregation
steps.instruction: Add the desired concentration of PAF (2.6 × 10⁻⁸–2.6 × 10⁻⁵ M) or thrombin (0.01–1 mU/µL) to the PRP cuvette, record the light‑transmission aggregation curve, and use the latent curve (100 % aggregation) as reference for evaluating agonists or antiplatelet compounds.
